text: Twin-field QKD beats the PLOB bound at long distance, achieving a rate that scales as the square root of the channel transmittance. What is the origin of this sqrt(eta) scaling?
choices: It uses quantum repeaters with quantum memories at each node
Alice and Bob each send dim phase-locked fields to an untrusted midpoint where they interfere, so only one photon need survive half the path — giving sqrt(eta) instead of eta
It amplifies the signal at the midpoint with a phase-sensitive amplifier
It encodes many bits per photon using high-dimensional states
explanation: In TF-QKD a single detector click at the untrusted midpoint heralds a key bit, and because only one photon must traverse half the distance the rate scales as sqrt(eta), overtaking PLOB beyond a few hundred km (record: 1,002 km). Choice 0 confuses it with repeaters — TF-QKD needs no quantum memory; choice 2 would violate no-cloning; choice 3 is a different idea that does not change the loss scaling.
